title: Roll back a partial render when done --render fails
lead: `done --render` puts the previous status back in memory when rendering raises, and it does not save the index. `render.write` can already have replaced some files.
**Not in this slice:** the default save-then-exit-1 policy, `--require-render` on other commands, or the TUI.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `render.write` writes each changed file in turn and deletes generated orphans in turn. If it raises after the first write, `.slicer/render/` matches neither the old roadmap nor the new one, while the slice status on disk is still the old one. `slicer check` then fails until someone re-renders. `--require-render` never wraps `done`, because that command renders before it publishes. The tests patch `render.write` to raise before any write, so they do not cover a failure mid-loop.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `done --render` whose render write raises `OSError` after at least one file has been replaced leaves every render file byte-for-byte as it was before the command. The item status, index, and log are unchanged. The exit is 2 and the code is `render` (today that `OSError` leaves the process as exit 3, `code="io"`). Sorted writes replace `ROADMAP.html` before `ROADMAP.md`, so the test has to fail on the first file.
2. A successful `done --render` still moves the slice, saves the index, and writes the new render output.
3. `--require-render` on a non-done command still restores its own snapshot. This slice does not change that path.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Make the `done --render` write atomic from the caller's point of view: either stage the new bytes and publish them after every write succeeds, or snapshot the render directory and restore it when `render.write` or `render.plan` raises. Restore has to cover files the failed write already replaced and files it already deleted. Wrap that `OSError` as `RenderError` so the exit stays 2. Keep the in-memory status rollback. Do not start saving the index before the render succeeds. `--require-render` does not need to wrap `done` once this path restores the render tree itself.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The three cases above pass, including a forced failure after the first `write_bytes`. The suite and `slicer check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. Do not tag or push.
